ruling.explanation:
Rider and driver: this dispute is decided on the trip's own GPS trace and the fare arithmetic, and it produces a partial refund of SGD 9.15 to the rider. Deviation. The GPS trace EV-GPS-09111 (weight 1.0; 205 fixes at 10-second intervals, 100% coverage, no gaps) measures 16.2 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff; the booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-09111 is 12.0 km. The excess is 4.2 km, or 35.0% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass (above 20% and above 0.8 km), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. It does not reach the 50% / 8.0 km materiality gates, so it is not MATERIAL: no POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is required, no FULL_REFUND uplift is available, and no driver-conduct referral arises. The trace is unimpaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), so the deviation stands on the trace alone and no corroboration is needed. The driver's answer. The statement that he 'followed the road available to me' is an external-cause assertion with no advisory behind it. The only traffic artifact, EV-ADVIS-09111-01, is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and covers nothing, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run and, under POL-RD-13, the assertion carries no weight. Because no advisory evidence ID was cited, this is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. No rider-requested detour was made: the rider's only message asks the driver to return to the booked route, and no endpoint was amended, so POL-RD-04 and POL-RD-05 do not apply. The refund. The fare model is METERED and there is no quoted fare, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and POL-RD-02 governs. Recomputed fare on the booked optimal = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 12.0 km + 0.28 x 24.0 min) x 1.2 surge (read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) = 23.424, + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP for the on-optimal Pioneer Road inbound gantry - 1.00 promo discount = 24.224. Charged total = 33.36. Refund = 33.36 - 24.224 = 9.136, rounded up to SGD 9.15. ERP. The Tuas South Avenue 8 loop line (2.00) is off-route pass-through; it is itemised here for transparency but is already comprehended in the recomputed fare, which includes only on-route gantries, so it is NOT added on top of the 9.15 (POL-RD-09(1)). The Pioneer Road inbound line (1.00) is properly chargeable and sits inside the recomputed fare. Outcome. The refund is above the 0.50 de minimis and is 27.4% of the charged total, below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. It happens to equal the whole contested amount, but POL-RD-02's test for a full refund is the share of the charged total, which is not met. No driver compensation is due: the distance billed (16.2 km) equals the trace distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall under POL-RD-04. No profile field other than deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d is used as a ground of decision; the remaining profile data is context only.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

Both sides have run the same arithmetic, and it decides the case. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km — 11.5 km, not the rounded trip_record copy — against the booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km, or 15.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal_distance_km AND 0.8 km in absolute terms, and the two limbs are conjunctive. The 0.8 km limb passes; the 20% limb (2.0 km) does not, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's claimed figure of 1.69 is the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and it does not arise: POL-RD-02 runs only after a POL-RD-01 finding. For transparency, the arithmetic it describes would have been charged_total 19.39 less recomputed_fare 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to 1.70, but it is not an entitlement here and the rider's advocate rightly does not press it. No billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) is available either: the ERP total is 0.00 with an empty gantry list and the airport surcharge is 0.00, so no charge line is unmatched to the trace and the 'save for' route in POL-RD-01 opens nothing. The exculpatory clauses the driver might reach for — POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-12 — do not run, and nothing turns on that: because the excess fails the POL-RD-01 threshold the rider never shifts the burden under POL-RD-08, so the driver's denial (which cites no evidence ID) needs no corroboration and its silence costs nothing. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09112-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact; because no party asserts an external traffic cause or cites that identifier, POL-RD-13 governs — the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (133 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gap above 30 seconds, 100% coverage), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged either, and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. No referral issues: the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation test is not met (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 610) and there is no billing-integrity finding to record. Outcome: NO_ACTION. On this rider-filed dispute the present state stands — payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00, and no charge or refund moves. Confidence 0.95, above the 0.70 floor, resting on the gps_trace and trip_record, each at full weight 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties — this is a partial refund.

Agreed and on the record: an LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-09113-01) closed the Pelton Canal Link eastbound connector, the segment the booked optimal route used, from 18:14 to 18:55 on 20 September 2026, covering this trip, and it records the shortest lawful alternative between the booked endpoints as 12.0 km. The driver took the signed industrial diversion and told the rider at 18:22:40; the rider replied at 18:23:10, 'please take the lawful diversion.'

1. Deviation established (POL-RD-01). The GPS trace governs: 18.0 km (EV-GPS-09113 trace_distance_km) against the booked optimal of 10.0 km (EV-TRIP-09113) is an excess of 8.0 km and 80%, passing both tests. The trip_record's rounded copy happens to agree; that does not change which field decides.

2. The closure excuses only part of it (POL-RD-03). The advisory names a road the optimal route traverses and its window covers the trip, so the driver is exonerated — but the exoneration is capped at the lesser of the measured excess (8.0 km) and 1.30 x (12.0 - 10.0) + 1.00 = 3.60 km. So 3.60 km is excused and 4.40 km is not. The closure-adjusted optimal is 10.0 + 3.60 = 13.60 km, and its duration is 20.0 x 13.60/10.0 = 27.2 min. The driver's claim to that effect is accepted; the rider's point that 18.0 km exceeds even the 12.0 km lawful alternative is also accepted — it is exactly why the cap bites.

3. The refund is arithmetic (POL-RD-02). recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 13.60 + 0.28 x 27.2) x 1.0, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (EV-FARE-09113), + 0.80 platform fee + 1.00 ERP on the optimal route = 23.416. Charged_total is 31.42 (EV-FARE-09113). Refund = 31.42 - 23.416 = 8.004, rounded up to SGD 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and 25.5% of charged_total, far below the 90% that would force a full refund.

4. The off-route gantry is not added again (POL-RD-09(1)). The SGD 2.80 charged at the 'Industrial loop exit' gantry, which is off the optimal route, is already comprehended inside the SGD 8.05, exactly as both sides say; adding it would double-count the same money.

5. One fare line is a billing error (POL-RD-09(4)). The SGD 1.00 charged at the 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' gantry is a charge for a gantry this trip's GPS trace never passes: of the 205 fixes, the nearest comes 834.18 m from the gantry, well outside the 250 m match radius the clause prescribes. The driver's claim that this line is 'properly chargeable' and 'not a phantom charge' is rejected: the on_optimal_route flag and trip_record.optimal_route_erp_sgd show the line has a counterpart in the record, which answers POL-RD-10(8) escalation, but neither shows the vehicle actually crossed the gantry, which is what POL-RD-09(4) asks. The SGD 1.00 is refunded in full as a standalone correction, and the line is referred for billing-integrity review.

6. No repeat-deviation uplift, no conduct referral (POL-RD-06, POL-GEN-01). driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610 — the trailing-window counters the clause names, not the lifetime prior_deviation_flags. Neither limb of the pattern test is met. (Materiality is assessed on the excess remaining after adjustment, 4.40 km, which is 32% of the 13.60 km adjusted optimal and below the 8.0 km absolute limb, so the deviation is established but not material; even on the unadjusted 80% the profile check returns clean, so nothing turns on it. The rider's assertion of materiality is corrected on that basis.)

7. No rider-requested detour (POL-RD-04). The rider's message names no road or place and carries waypoint_hint null, so the 200 m corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable; in any event the instruction authorised only the 12.0 km lawful diversion, not 18.0 km.

8. No escalation (POL-RD-10). The trace is unimpaired — 205 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, maximum gap 0.0 s — so POL-RD-07 limbs (a)-(c) and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged; the identifier TRP-09113 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the refund is below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below charged_total; and the only fare line without a trace crossing is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes.

9. No relocation (POL-RD-05): pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so the booked optimal, as adjusted by POL-RD-03, is the baseline.

Outcome: the SGD 8.05 you contested is returned in full, and SGD 1.00 more is returned as the billing correction — SGD 9.05 in total. Confidence is 0.90; the deciding facts are carried by artifacts all at weight 1.0 (EV-GPS-09113, EV-TRIP-09113, EV-FARE-09113 and EV-ADVIS-09113-01), so the cap is 1.0, and no POL-GEN-02 discount applies.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing integrity: the SGD 1.00 'Pelton lawful diversion entry' ERP line charges a gantry this trip's gps_trace never passes (nearest of the 205 fixes is 834.18 m from the gantry, outside POL-RD-09(4)'s 250 m match radius); the line has been refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction and is referred for billing-integrity review.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties. This was an upfront-quoted trip: EV-FARE-09114 carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd SGD 22.00 against a total_charged of SGD 25.20, payment_status CHARGED. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The measured excess is established but not material: EV-GPS-09114's governing trace_distance_km is 16.0 km against the booked optimal 12.5 km — 3.5 km, or 28.00% — which clears POL-RD-01's 0.8 km and 20% gates but falls below the 8.0 km and 50% material gates, so no POL-RD-06 materiality, uplift or conduct referral follows. The driver's claims to that effect are accepted.

The one live item is the ERP line, and there the driver does not contest the rider's point. EV-FARE-09114 bills SGD 3.20 for the gantry 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' (lat 1.34, lng 103.78). EV-GPS-09114 places the trace's closest approach 7,482.07 m from that gantry (fix index 65, 2026-09-21T11:40:50), with on_optimal_route false and gap_brackets_closest_approach false — roughly thirty times POL-RD-09(4)'s 250 m crossing radius. The driver's own counterparty statement records that he 'did not see or pass the gantry named on the receipt'. That is a phantom pass-through line: a billing-integrity failure refunded in full under POL-RD-09(4), and equally the rider's remedy under POL-RD-11(a) and (b).

The amount is read off the fare breakdown: charged_total 25.20 less quoted_fare 22.00 less properly chargeable pass-throughs 0.00 = SGD 3.20, which is the published pol_rd_11_remedy and rounds (up to the nearest SGD 0.05) to SGD 3.20. The whole contested amount is returned, so the outcome for the filing party is FULL_REFUND. POL-RD-09(1) and POL-RD-11(b) forbid counting the off-route line twice: the refund is SGD 3.20, not SGD 6.40.

No further money moves in either direction, so the driver's remaining points are accepted: distance_charged_km 16.0 equals trace_distance_km 16.0, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall above 1.0 km and no POL-RD-04 compensation; and the POL-RD-06 pattern test fails on the driver's own profile (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 610 completed trips in 90 days), so no repeat-deviation pattern is established.

No escalation. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 169 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, max_gap_sec 0.0, coverage 100%, admissibility COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged. Trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown (TRP-09114). The only unmatched charge line is the one refunded under POL-RD-09(4), which POL-RD-09(4) and POL-RD-10(8) expressly exclude from escalation. Confidence rests on EV-GPS-09114 and EV-FARE-09114, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and the 0.70 floor is not approached.

The phantom ERP charge is recorded as a billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4). That referral rides with the monetary ruling and neither displaces nor delays it.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4): billing-integrity review — the fare_breakdown (EV-FARE-09114) charged SGD 3.20 for the 'Bukit Merah Central westbound' ERP gantry, which the GPS trace (EV-GPS-09114) never crossed (closest fix 7,482.07 m away, on_optimal_route false); the line was refunded in full as a standalone pass-through correction.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the one fact that decides this case: the GPS trace for trip TRP-09115 is broken. EV-GPS-09115 carries admissibility status IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.6 and issue code GPS_GAP, with a 160-second break between fixes from 20:03:10 to 20:05:50 SGT — and that break falls inside the very stretch the rider disputes. That is longer than the 90 seconds POL-RD-07(a) allows, so the trace is impaired for policy purposes as well as for the admissibility pre-pass; those are two separate findings and I make both. On the numbers the excess is 4.0 km, or 36.4%, over the booked optimal of 11.0 km on EV-TRIP-09115, with the trace figure of 15.0 km governing under POL-RD-01 — comfortably over both POL-RD-01 gates — but POL-RD-07(ii) says a deviation may not be established on an impaired trace alone.

It must then be corroborated by one of the four independent sources POL-RD-07(ii) names, and none is present. The chat log, EV-CHAT-09115 (weight 1.0), contains no driver admission of a detour: at 20:08:20 the rider writes that the route display 'jumped and now shows us away from the booked road', and at 20:08:50 the driver replies only that his own navigation display 'also refreshed' and that he 'continued toward the destination'. That is not a concession that the vehicle left the booked road, and an admission built on what the driver did not say is not an admission. The fare breakdown, EV-FARE-09115 (weight 1.0), charges no ERP gantries at all, so no gantry places the vehicle on a corridor the optimal route does not use. The driver's counterparty statement denies an extra stop and a detour request rather than admitting a route, and it carries no weight_multiplier in any event. And trip_record.actual_distance_km of 15.0 km on EV-TRIP-09115 is, by POL-RD-01's own words, a rounded convenience copy of the same trace measurement — not a source independent of it.

Two rider points do not change that. First, the argument that the excess survives whether the gap stretch is taken as the straight line between its bounding fixes (1.35 km, consistent with 160 seconds at the trace's single 30 kph speed) or removed altogether (leaving about 2.65 km / 24.1%): the arithmetic is right, but the residual is still measured from the impaired trace, and POL-RD-07(ii) forbids establishing the deviation on that trace alone. Second, the rider's POL-RD-02 computation is sound — recomputed_fare 20.831 = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.0 + 0.28 x 22.0) x 1.1) + 0.80, giving 26.60 - 20.831 = 5.769, rounded up to 5.80 — but it runs only where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01, which this record does not do. No pass-through correction is due either: EV-FARE-09115 itemises no ERP, no toll, no airport surcharge and no waiting-time fee, so POL-RD-09 has nothing to carry. The driver-favouring excuses under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 all likewise fail to engage, but their failure does not fill the gap in the rider's evidence.

The missing traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09115-01 (status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT), is not the deciding defect and does not itself escalate the case: no party cited an advisory identifier, and POL-RD-13 provides that the absence of an uncited advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) contradiction. What governs is the trace itself.

The trigger that fired is POL-RD-10(3): the GPS trace is impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and no corroborating artifact of the kind POL-RD-07(ii) names exists. POL-RD-07(iii) directs the same outcome — absence of proof here is a data failure, not a finding for the driver, so this is not a NO_ACTION. My confidence is capped at 0.6, the weight of the impaired trace the ruling rests on (POL-GEN-02(2)), and that is also below the 0.70 platform floor (POL-RD-10(1)). Escalation is terminal: no money moves, and the disputed SGD 5.80 is held rather than collected or refunded. What would resolve the case is the raw fixes inside the 20:03:10-20:05:50 window, an independent record of the route such as an ERP gantry charged on a corridor the optimal route does not use, or a traffic advisory covering the trip window. I issue no referral: the deviation is not material and no repeat pattern is established, so POL-RD-06(c) does not fire; no charge line is unmatched, so POL-RD-09(4) does not fire; and no no-show clause is in play.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
